get.description:
Redirects the customer to Google's account picker / consent screen. This is the
"Sign in with Google" **button** flow — three navigations (site → Google → back). For the
one-click, no-navigation alternative, see `POST /google/one-tap` below.

Absolute origin to complete the login on instead of the server's default FRONTEND_URL — e.g. so a developer testing from localhost:3000 doesn't get bounced to the live site. Must exactly match an entry in the backend's trusted-origins allowlist (the same one used for CORS); silently ignored (falls back to FRONTEND_URL) if absent or not allowlisted. Ask backend to add a new origin — this is not something the frontend can widen on its own.

post.description:
**What this is.** Google One Tap renders a small prompt (top corner of the page) showing the
visitor's actual Google account, if their browser already has an active Google session. Signing in
never navigates away from the page — contrast with `GET /google` above, which is a full
site → Google → site redirect chain. This endpoint is the *second half* of that flow: it takes the
credential Google's own script hands to the page and turns it into a customer session, the same way
`GET /google/callback` does for the redirect flow (same underlying service call, same
account-linking rules, same staff-email block) — just without the authorization-code round trip,
because the browser already has a signed proof of identity from Google directly.

---

### Why this can't be a server-only integration

Detecting "is this browser already signed into Google" happens inside Google's own iframe/FedCM
context, in the browser. There is no server-side equivalent. The credential this endpoint accepts
is the artifact of that browser-side detection — a signed Google ID token (a JWT), not an
authorization code. So the frontend *must* run Google's Identity Services script and collect the
credential client-side; this endpoint only ever verifies and exchanges what the browser already
obtained.

---

### Implementation sequence (frontend)

1. **Load Google's script** (`https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client`) once, e.g. in the root
   layout. Skip all of this entirely if `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` isn't set, or if the
   visitor already has a session (check your existing session cookie first — don't prompt someone
   who's already signed in).
2. **Mint a nonce yourself, server-side**, before initializing the prompt. This has to happen on
   *your* server (a Next.js route handler, etc.), not in client JS — a nonce the browser could
   generate/inspect isn't binding to anything. Store it in an httpOnly cookie scoped to the page/
   route that will use it, single-use.
3. **Initialize Google's prompt** with that nonce and `use_fedcm_for_prompt: true`. Set
   `auto_select: false` unless you specifically want Google to skip the prompt and sign a
   single-account visitor in silently.
4. **On the credential callback** Google fires when the visitor accepts: send `{ credential, nonce }`
   to *your own* backend route (not directly to this API — see the JSON-body note below), which
   forwards it to `POST /api/auth/customer/google/one-tap`.
5. **On a 200**, read `accessToken` / `refreshToken` / `expiresIn` from the body and set them as
   your own first-party httpOnly cookies (same shape/names your existing auth flow already uses),
   then refetch whatever query drives your signed-in header state. No page navigation needed.
6. **On any 4xx**, fail quietly — log it, don't show an error to the visitor. One Tap is an
   enhancement over the existing "Sign in" button, not a replacement; that button must keep working
   even if every One Tap attempt fails.

---

### The nonce is not optional

Google signs whatever nonce value the client passed it *into* the ID token itself, as the token's
own `nonce` claim. This endpoint checks that claim against the `nonce` field in the request body —
**not** against anything stored server-side on the backend; the binding lives entirely inside the
signed JWT. That means:
- The nonce your frontend sends here must be the *exact* value passed to Google's `initialize()`
  call for the prompt that produced this specific `credential`.
- If you skip this (send an empty/omitted nonce, or one that doesn't match), a captured/replayed
  credential would otherwise be valid for its full ID-token lifetime (~1 hour) — this check is what
  prevents that, not a nice-to-have.
- Generate the nonce server-side and mirror it into an httpOnly cookie, single-use, so the page
  itself never had the ability to choose or predict the value it sends back.

---

### Why JSON body, not Set-Cookie

The browser never calls this backend endpoint directly — your frontend's *own server-side* route
handler does (it's the one holding the nonce cookie and calling Google). A `Set-Cookie` header from
this response would land on this API's origin, not your storefront's, and be useless to the browser.
Tokens come back in the JSON body specifically so your route handler can turn them into cookies on
the correct (your) origin.

---

### Non-backend prerequisites — this 404s/401s until these are done

- **Google Cloud Console**, same OAuth client as `GOOGLE_CUSTOMER_CLIENT_ID`: add your storefront

Postgres-backed product listing with full filter and pagination support. Unlike GET /search (which uses OpenSearch), this endpoint queries the database directly via Prisma.

**Primary use case:** Internal admin dashboard — product browsing, filtering by category+brand, and selecting products for operations like markup rule application.

**Frontend workflow for markup rules:**
1. Staff navigates to the markup rules page
2. Staff selects a category from a dropdown (populated by GET /categories)
3. Staff selects a brand from a dropdown (populated by GET /brands)
4. Frontend calls this endpoint with `categoryId` and/or `brandId` to show matching products
5. Staff sees the filtered product list with prices
6. Staff enters a markup percentage and clicks "Preview" (POST /pricing/markup-rules/preview)
7. Staff reviews projected prices, then clicks "Create Rule & Apply"

**Why use this instead of GET /search?**
- GET /search uses OpenSearch — designed for customer-facing full-text search with facets
- GET /all uses Prisma/Postgres directly — simpler, no OpenSearch dependency, better for internal admin filtering where you just need exact category+brand matches
- Both support the same query parameters, but /all is more reliable for admin operations since it reads directly from the database (no indexing delay)

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| q | string | — | Free-text search (matches product name and description, case-insensitive) |
| categoryId | uuid | — | Filter by category UUID — matches this category AND any of its subcategories |
| categorySlug | string | — | Filter by category slug (alternative to categoryId) — same subcategory-inclusive matching |
| brandId | uuid | — | Filter by exact brand UUID |

This runs **asynchronously** in a separate OpenSearch worker process — NOT in the API process. The endpoint only *queues* the job and returns **202 immediately**. There is **no batchId and no progress handle** — unlike POST /bulk, you cannot poll this for completion. Only one full sync can be queued at a time (the job is deduplicated by a fixed jobId, so repeated clicks are harmless no-ops).

## Frontend implementation

- Render this action **only** for users whose role has the `search:admin` permission.
- On the **202** response, show a non-blocking toast: *"Catalog sync started — runs in the background, may take a few minutes for a large catalog."*
- **Do NOT show a progress bar or a spinner that waits for completion** — no completion event is coming back.
- **Disable the button for a short cooldown** (~30–60s). The backend dedupes anyway, but a disabled state stops the user wondering if their click registered.
- To later confirm the index is healthy, compare OpenSearch `_count` against the active product count in Postgres (requires a separate status endpoint — not yet implemented).

## chunkSize

Optional. Controls how many products are read + bulk-indexed per batch. Larger = faster but more memory per batch; smaller = gentler on memory. Omit the body entirely (or send `{}`) to use the default of **100**.

## When to use

After first deploy, after a mapping change + reindex, or any time search has drifted from the database.

Requires `search:admin` permission.

- Gate it behind the `search:admin` permission.

Busts the **Redis** cache for products. This is a different concern from indexing — it does **NOT** touch the OpenSearch index. It clears cached search results, cached product pages, and the cached category/brand lists so the next request rebuilds them fresh from the database.

## Behaviour: synchronous

Unlike /admin/sync and /admin/reindex (which queue async jobs and return 202), this one **does the work inline** and returns **200** only once the cache is actually cleared. So a normal *spinner → success* pattern is correct here — by the time you get the response, it's done.

| Body | Effect |
|---|---|
| `{ "productId": "<uuid>" }` | Clears cache for **just that one product** (its by-id and by-slug keys). |
| `{}` (or omit body) | Clears the **entire** product cache: all cached search results, all product pages, and the featured / category-tree / brand-list caches. |

- Gate behind `search:admin`.
- This is the one admin action where a blocking spinner is appropriate — await the 200, then show success.
- Make clear to the user this clears **cache only**: if search results are wrong because the *index* is stale, they need /admin/reindex or /admin/sync instead, not this.

Creates a new percentage-based markup rule, scoped EITHER to a category+brand combination OR (NEW) to one exact product.

**Percentage range:** minimum 2%, maximum 500%. Negative values are not allowed — to reduce prices for traffic, lower the percentage toward 2%, not below.

**Important:** Creating a rule does NOT retroactively change any existing product prices. It only affects:
1. Future product creations (POST /products) — NOT applicable to product-scoped rules, since the product must already exist to reference its id (see below)
2. Future variant additions (POST /:productId/variants)
3. Future pricing updates (PATCH /variants/:variantId/pricing)

To apply the rule to existing products, call POST /pricing/markup-rules/apply after creating the rule.

**NEW — exact-product scoping:** send `productId` instead of `categoryId`/`brandId` to pin a markup to one exact product, overriding whatever category/brand rule would otherwise apply to it:
```json
{ "productId": "<uuid>", "markupPercentage": 15, "applyTo": "PRICE", "notes": "Flagship SKU — higher margin" }
```
`productId` is **mutually exclusive** with `categoryId`/`brandId` — sending both is a 422 validation error, since the product already implies its own category/brand and mixing them would be ambiguous about which one drives resolution. A product must already exist before you can create a rule for it (this is an edit-time action on an existing product, not part of the product-creation form).

**Rule specificity (when multiple rules could match), most specific first:**
1. **Exact product** (`productId`) — NEW, highest priority. Checked and returned before category/brand tiers are evaluated at all, so a product-specific rule can never conflict with your existing category/brand rules.
2. Exact match (categoryId + brandId)
3. Brand-only (categoryId is null) — matches all categories for that brand
4. Category-only (brandId is null) — matches all brands in that category

**Category hierarchy:** If a product is in a subcategory and no rule exists for that subcategory, the system walks up to the parent category automatically. (Not applicable to product-scoped rules — there's no hierarchy to walk for a single product.)

**Constraint:** Only one rule per (categoryId, brandId, productId) combination. Attempting to create a duplicate — including a second rule for the same `productId` — returns an error suggesting to update the existing rule instead.

The response includes `variantsRecomputed` showing how many were updated. For a category/brand rule this is the category-wide pricing dial; for a product-scoped rule (NEW) it recomputes just that one product's variants — raise the percentage to widen margin, lower it (min 2%) to drive traffic.

You cannot change a rule's scope (`productId`/`categoryId`/`brandId`) via this endpoint — delete and recreate the rule instead.

**Partial update:** Only include the fields you want to change. Changing only notes or isActive does not trigger a recompute.

**Important:** Deleting a rule does NOT revert any prices that were previously adjusted by this rule. Prices that were already marked up remain at their current values. To undo a markup, lower the rule's percentage back down (minimum 2%) — prices recompute from base automatically — or deactivate the rule (PATCH with `isActive: false`) to keep the audit trail.

post.summary: Cancel markup rule and reset all prices to base
post.description:
The primary "undo" action for a markup rule. Does two things atomically in a single operation:

1. **Deactivates the rule** — sets `isActive = false` so future product creations, variant additions, and price edits in this category+brand (or, NEW, exact-product) scope no longer have the markup applied automatically.
2. **Resets all prices to base** — walks every active variant and part in the rule's scope and writes `price = basePrice`, `compareAtPrice = baseCompareAtPrice`.

After this call, prices are back at the values staff originally entered — the markup is fully undone. The rule record stays in the database for audit purposes (who created it, what percentage, when it ran, when it was cancelled).

---

## When to use this vs. other endpoints

| Situation | Endpoint to use |
|---|---|
| "I'm done with this price increase — undo it" | **This endpoint** ← use this 99% of the time |
| "Reset prices temporarily but keep the rule active for later" | POST /pricing/markup-rules/:ruleId/reset |
| "Reset a category that has no rule, or whose rule was already deleted" | POST /pricing/reset-category |
| "Remove the rule record from the database entirely" | DELETE /pricing/markup-rules/:ruleId |

---

## Why deactivate before resetting?

Order matters. The service deactivates the rule and clears the resolver cache **before** writing the new prices. This closes a race condition: if the rule were still active while prices were being written, a concurrent variant edit by another staff member could re-apply the markup to that variant mid-reset, leaving one variant at the marked-up price while everything else is at base. Deactivating first ensures the rule cannot fire again during or after the reset.

---

## What "base price" means

`basePrice` is the permanent anchor — the price staff originally entered when creating or last manually updating a variant. It is **never modified** by markup operations. Every markup derives from it (`price = basePrice × (1 + percentage / 100)`), so markups never compound on top of each other. After cancelling:

```
Before markup was applied:
  basePrice = ₦10,000   price = ₦10,000

After +20% rule applied:
  basePrice = ₦10,000   price = ₦12,000   ← basePrice untouched

After cancel:
  basePrice = ₦10,000   price = ₦10,000   ← restored from base
```

---

## Can I apply a new rule after cancelling?

Yes. Because `basePrice` is always preserved, you can cancel this rule and immediately create and apply a new rule at a different percentage. The new markup will derive cleanly from the same base:

```
Cancel +20% rule  →  prices at ₦10,000
Create +35% rule  →  apply it  →  prices at ₦13,500
Cancel +35% rule  →  prices at ₦10,000 again
```

---

## Scope

The reset covers the same scope as the rule itself:
- **NEW — product-scoped rules:** if the rule has `productId` set, the reset covers exactly that one product's active variants — no category walk, since the scope is a single product.
- Otherwise: all **active variants** of **active products** where `product.categoryId` matches the rule's category (including direct subcategories one level deep)
- Optionally narrowed by `brandId` if the rule has one set
- All **active parts** that carry the rule's `categoryId` + `brandId` directly (never applicable to product-scoped rules — product markup never touches parts)

Brand-only rules (where both `categoryId` and `productId` are null on the rule) cannot be reset by this endpoint — use POST /pricing/reset-category with just a `brandId` for that case.

---

## Side effects

After resetting prices the endpoint automatically:
- Invalidates Redis cache for all affected products and variants
- Updates the denormalized `minPrice` / `maxPrice` fields on each affected product
- Queues an OpenSearch re-index job for each affected product so the search index reflects the new prices immediately
- Busts the markup rule resolver cache so the deactivated rule is no longer returned for new price computations

---

## Rate limit

Shared with the reset endpoint: **10 cancel/reset operations per hour per staff member**.

---

## Example — full admin UI workflow

```
1. Staff opens the markup rules table  →  GET /pricing/markup-rules
2. Staff sees rule MKP-XXXXXXXX: "Laptops + Dell, +20%, active"
3. Staff clicks "Reset to default price"
4. Frontend calls:

   POST /api/v1/products/pricing/markup-rules/<rule-db-uuid>/cancel
   Authorization: Bearer <staff-token>

   (no request body required)

5. Response:
   {
     "success": true,
     "data": {
       "variantsReset": 24,
       "partsReset": 0
     }
   }

6. Frontend shows: "24 variants reset to base price"
   (partsReset is always 0 — product markup never affects product parts)
7. Rule is now inactive in the table — staff can delete it or re-activate it later
```

Adds a variant to the cart, or increases its quantity if already present (capped at 100 per item).

**Identifying what to add — send one of:**

| Field | When to use |
|---|---|
| `variantId` | User selected a specific variant (size, color, condition). Preferred. |
| `productId` | Product has one variant, or you want the server to auto-select. |

The server picks the best active variant using availability priority: `IN_STOCK (5) → LOW_STOCK (4) → PREORDER (3) → OUT_OF_STOCK (2) → DISCONTINUED (1)`. Ties are broken by lowest price. If the best available variant is `OUT_OF_STOCK` or `DISCONTINUED` a `400` is returned.

**Stock enforcement:**
Checks `stockQuantity − reservedQuantity` (net available). If the variant is already in the cart the quantities are summed and re-checked before the cap of 100 is applied.

---

## Complete frontend payment flow

```
1. Customer clicks "Pay Now"
         ↓
2. Frontend calls POST /api/v1/payments/initiate
   (include idempotencyKey + orderId in body)
         ↓
3. Backend returns { paymentUrl, paymentId, providerReference }
         ↓
4. Frontend redirects customer to paymentUrl
   (Miden or Paystack hosted checkout page — card entry happens there)
         ↓
5. Customer completes payment on hosted page
         ↓
6. Miden/Paystack redirects customer back to your callbackUrl
   e.g. https://yoursite.com/payment/callback?reference=MDN-1A2B3C4D-E5F6A7B8
         ↓
7. Frontend calls GET /api/v1/payments/verify/{reference}
   to confirm the final status
         ↓
8. If status === "PAID" → show success screen, clear cart
   If status === "FAILED" → show error, let customer retry
   If status === "PENDING" → show "processing" message, poll /api/v1/payments/{paymentId}
```

---

## Gateway selection

The `gateway` field is optional. The server default is **Miden**.

| gateway field in body | Which gateway is used |
|---|---|
| omitted | Miden (server default) |
| `"miden"` | Miden |
| `"paystack"` | Paystack |

---

## Idempotency key

You must generate a unique `idempotencyKey` per payment attempt. If the request is retried (network error, double-click), the server returns the same result instead of creating a duplicate payment.

Rules:
- 16–100 characters
- Only alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores
- Must be different for each new payment attempt (but the same on a retry of the same attempt)

**Generate one client-side:**
```ts
const idempotencyKey = `pay-${orderId.slice(0,8)}-${Date.now()}`;
// e.g. "pay-a1b2c3d4-1720000000000"
```

---

## CSRF

Whether you need a CSRF token depends on **how you authenticate**:

### If you use `Authorization: Bearer` → no CSRF token needed
A Bearer-authenticated request can't be forged cross-site, so CSRF is skipped. Do not send `X-CSRF-Token`.

```ts
fetch('/api/v1/payments/initiate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
    'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey,
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ orderId, idempotencyKey, callbackUrl }),
});
```

### If you use **cookie auth** (`customerAccessToken` cookie) → double-submit CSRF required
The browser auto-sends your auth cookie, so a CSRF token is required. Because the API and the SPA are on different origins, JS can't read the API's `csrf-token` cookie directly — so fetch the token from `GET /api/v1/payments/csrf-token` (it returns the value in the body **and** sets the cookie), then echo it as `X-CSRF-Token`.

```ts
// 1. Once (e.g. after login): get the CSRF token
const { data } = await fetch('/api/v1/payments/csrf-token', {
  credentials: 'include',            // sends + receives cookies
}).then(r => r.json());
const csrfToken = data.csrfToken;

// 2. On each payment call: send it as a header, with credentials
fetch('/api/v1/payments/initiate', {
  method: 'POST',
  credentials: 'include',            // browser sends auth + csrf-token cookies
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'X-CSRF-Token': csrfToken,       // must match the csrf-token cookie
    'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey,
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ orderId, idempotencyKey, callbackUrl }),
});
```

`403 { "error": "CSRF token missing" }` means you're on cookie auth but didn't send `X-CSRF-Token`; `403 { "error": "CSRF validation failed" }` means the header didn't match the cookie (re-fetch the token).

---

## Full request / response example

**Request body:**
```json
{
  "orderId": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "idempotencyKey": "pay-a1b2c3d4-1720000000000",
  "callbackUrl": "https://yoursite.com/payment/callback"
}
```

**Successful response (201):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "paymentId": "PMT-A1B2C3D4E5F6A7B8C9D0",
    "paymentUrl": "https://www.sandbox.midencards.io/pay/checkout?paymentReference=84f1ba8f",
    "accessCode": "",
    "providerReference": "MDN-1A2B3C4D-E5F6A7B8",
    "amount": 15000,
    "currency": "NGN",
    "gateway": "miden"
  }
}
```

**What to do with the response:**
```ts
const { paymentUrl, paymentId, providerReference } = data;

// 1. Save paymentId and providerReference locally (sessionStorage is fine)
sessionStorage.setItem('pendingPaymentId', paymentId);
sessionStorage.setItem('pendingPaymentRef', providerReference);

// 2. Redirect customer to the hosted checkout
window.location.href = paymentUrl;
```

---

## If a PENDING payment already exists for the order

The server returns the existing payment session instead of creating a new one.
This is safe — just redirect the customer to the returned `paymentUrl` again.

---

## Rate limit
5 initiation attempts per customer per 15 minutes. Blocked for 30 minutes after that.

**This is a staff-only record-keeping endpoint — it does NOT trigger an automatic bank refund.**

---

## When to use

1. Customer requests a refund
2. Staff processes the bank transfer / cash refund manually
3. Staff logs into the admin panel and calls this endpoint to record the refund
4. The customer's payment record is updated to `REFUNDED` (full) or stays `PAID` with a refund entry (partial)

Always supply a unique `idempotencyKey` per refund attempt. If the staff member submits twice, only one refund is recorded.

|---|---|
| Only paid payments | Payment status must be `PAID` or `REFUNDED` (partial) |
| Cannot over-refund | Sum of all refunds cannot exceed the original payment amount |
| Omit amount for full refund | If `amount` is omitted, the full remaining balance is refunded |

**Frontend does NOT call this.** Miden calls it automatically when a payment settles.

When a customer pays on the Miden hosted checkout page, Miden sends a webhook to this endpoint.
The backend verifies the HMAC-SHA256 signature, deduplicates the event, and queues it for processing.
Once processed, the payment status in the database is updated to `PAID` or `FAILED`.

**This is why polling `GET /payments/{paymentId}` eventually returns `PAID`.**

**Signature header:** `x-signature` — 64-character lowercase HMAC-SHA256 hex.
**Signed over:** `${eventId}&${eventTime}` from the payload body.

**Response body reflects what actually happened**, not just a bare acknowledgement:
- No signature header at all → `200 { received: false, reason: '...' }` — treated as a reachability probe (Miden's own webhook-subscribe endpoint pings this URL before accepting a registration), never as a real event.
- Valid signature, new event → `200 { received: true, outcome: 'enqueued', eventId, eventType, gateway }`.
- Valid signature, already-processed event (24h dedup window) → `200 { received: true, outcome: 'duplicate', eventId, eventType, gateway }`.
- Valid signature, event type this backend doesn't act on → `200 { received: true, outcome: 'ignored_event_type', eventId, eventType, gateway }`.

Note `outcome: 'enqueued'` means the event passed signature/dedup checks and was queued — it does NOT yet mean the payment was finalized (that happens asynchronously in the worker). Check `GET /payments/{paymentId}` or `GET /verify/{reference}` for the final outcome.

200.description: See description — response body outcome varies (probe ack, enqueued, duplicate, or ignored event type).

401.description: Invalid HMAC signature (present but malformed) — Miden will not retry.

Re-enqueues a dead-lettered job's original payload onto the live payment-events queue, then removes it from the DLQ.

Safe to call even if you're not sure the underlying issue was actually fixed — VERIFY and WEBHOOK jobs both route through idempotent functions (a payment already `PAID` short-circuits immediately), so replaying a still-broken job just dead-letters it again rather than double-applying any payment side-effect (no duplicate charge, no duplicate refund).

**Note on why a DLQ entry exists at all:** the DLQ only ever contains jobs that *threw an exception* after exhausting every retry. A job that completed without error but still failed to resolve a payment (e.g. couldn't match a gateway reference to a Payment row) does NOT appear here — that failure mode is instead caught by the separate stuck-PENDING reconciliation sweep, which alerts staff directly rather than going through the DLQ.

Registers/overwrites the URL Miden delivers Card and Virtual Account collection events to (Miden's `PATCH /api/v1/webhook/subscribe`). Both event types are pointed at the SAME endpoint here — this backend already dispatches by payload shape, not by which URL received it.

Runs entirely server-side using this deployment's own `MIDEN_CLIENT_ID`/`MIDEN_CLIENT_SECRET`/`MIDEN_UNIQUE_KEY`/`MIDEN_WEBHOOK_HASH` — nothing needs to be copied into a local shell or pasted anywhere to call this.

This is a one-time (or occasional, e.g. on domain change) setup step, not something called per-transaction. If webhooks have never been registered — or were registered against a stale URL — Miden simply has nowhere to send collection events, which looks identical to "webhook never fires" from the payment side, with no error anywhere in this codebase (there's nothing to error on — Miden just never calls).

**`baseUrl` is required.** It used to default to this request's own `protocol`+`host`, which is wrong behind a misconfigured reverse proxy (`req.protocol` can report `http` even when the public endpoint is HTTPS-only) and silently registers a broken webhook URL with no error anywhere — the worst kind of wrong, since it surfaces days later as unexplained stuck payments. The caller now must send the real public HTTPS base URL explicitly.

get.description:
## Verifying a transaction directly against Miden

*This endpoint is documentation only — there is nothing to call.* It covers the workflow behind `GET /miden/lookup/{reference}`: what it's for, which reference to pass, where the UI should surface it, and how the pieces fit together — for whoever's building or using the payments admin section.

### Why this exists

A payment's state in our own system can look wrong, stale, or stuck for reasons that have nothing to do with the payment itself — a webhook that never arrived, a reconciliation sweep that hasn't run yet, a page that hasn't been refreshed. `GET /miden/lookup/{reference}` exists to answer one question with certainty: **what does Miden itself actually have on record for this transaction, right now** — independent of anything cached, delayed, or unresolved on our side.

### The one thing to get right: which reference to use

Every Miden payment carries two different reference-shaped values, and only one of them means anything to Miden's own API:

| Reference | Where it lives | Works with `/miden/lookup`? |
|---|---|---|
| `providerReference` | This app's own generated value, e.g. `MDN-1785681105245-F08EEA391E88E156` | **No.** Miden does not recognize this string at all. |
| Miden's own reference | `gatewayResponse.reference` on the payment record, e.g. `56cbc0300ab1ce6ace76ded19b255f` | **Yes.** This is what Miden's own records are actually keyed on. |

Confirmed empirically: Miden's `Get Collections` records echo back **Miden's own** reference in the `merchantReference` field — not the value we originally sent when the payment was created, despite the field name. Searching with `providerReference` will scan every page and still find nothing, every time.

### Where the frontend should surface it

`gatewayResponse.reference` is captured once, at payment-link creation time, and is present on `GET /admin/transactions/{paymentId}`'s response for every Miden payment (also on `GET /payments/{paymentId}`, the customer-facing equivalent, for a customer's own payments).

**Render this value explicitly on the transaction detail view** — a labeled field (e.g. "Miden Reference"), ideally copyable. The goal: if a payment ever needs investigating, whoever's looking — support, staff, an engineer — already has the exact value needed without digging through raw `gatewayResponse` JSON, and it's identical to what a customer could read off their own receipt if it's ever shown to them.

### How the check itself works

```
GET /api/v1/payments/miden/lookup/{reference}
```

Pass Miden's reference (from `gatewayResponse.reference`, per above) as `{reference}`. This:

- Bypasses this app's own DB **entirely** — it never reads the local `Payment` row.
- Always hits Miden **live**. Unlike `GET /verify/{reference}`, it never short-circuits for an already-`PAID` payment, so it always reflects Miden's current real state at the exact moment you call it, not a cached one.
- Scans both channels — Get Collections (Cards), then falls back to Get Collections (Virtual Accounts) on a Cards miss — so it works the same way regardless of whether the payment was a card or a bank transfer.

This is the same tool used internally when a payment looks off: paste in the reference, get back exactly what Miden has on file right now — status, amount, whether the credit actually posted, the payment method. If our own system and Miden's disagree, this call is the tie-breaker.

### What it's for, and what it's not

- **Is for:** investigating one specific payment that looks wrong, stuck, or disputed. A deliberate, on-demand check.
- **Is not for:** routine polling or a general "transaction status" widget — it's a live external call to Miden, not a free local read. `GET /payments/{paymentId}` (local, fast, cached) is the right choice for normal status display; reach for this only when that's not enough to trust.

### One more thing, if you go further

If the lookup turns up a **Cards** transaction and it needs Miden to re-deliver the original webhook (recovery, not verification), the matched record's numeric `id` (in `rawResponse.id`, e.g. `1858`) is what `POST /miden/webhooks/resend` needs. This only works for Cards — confirmed directly against Miden's API that Virtual Account transactions (whose `id` is a UUID, not a number) cannot use this recovery path at all; Miden's own request validation rejects a non-numeric id before any of their business logic runs. For a stuck Virtual Account payment, the lookup above is still fully accurate for checking its state — there just isn't an equivalent "force a resend" action for that channel.

## Store tax (VAT) — TWO independent rule engines

There's a **global store-wide setting** — one `enabled` flag and one `rate` (%) — that acts as the
fallback for everything. On top of it there are **two completely separate, isolated rule tables**:

| Engine | Endpoint | Targets | Precedence tiers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TaxRule` | `/api/v1/tax/rules` | real **products** (exact SKU, category, brand) | 5 |
| `PartTaxRule` | `/api/v1/tax/part-rules` | **product parts** (exact part, category, brand, partType) | 8 |

They never cross over: a `TaxRule` scoped to category "Laptops" only ever matches genuine product
lines; a `PartTaxRule` scoped to category "RAM" only ever matches part lines, even if a part happens
to sit in a category that also has products in it. This mirrors the existing
`PriceMarkupRule` (products) vs `PartMarkupRule` (parts) split for pricing — same idea, applied to tax.

Tax is computed **per line item**, not once on the order total, because different items in the same
cart can resolve to different rates — and now, different *engines*.

### How a line is classified as "product" vs "part"
Every priced part is backed by a hidden internal product+variant that carries its price — that's
an implementation detail, not something the frontend needs to construct. What matters for the
frontend: each cart/order line already comes back with its own resolved `taxRate`/`taxAmount`/`taxSource`,
and `taxSource` tells you which engine and which tier answered — see the table below. You never need
to guess whether a line is a product or a part; read `taxSource`.

### `TaxRule` precedence (products) — most specific wins, resolver stops at first match
| # | Tier | `taxSource` value | Rule shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Specific product | `product` | `productId` set, category/brand null |
| 2 | Category + brand exact | `category+brand` | `categoryId` **and** `brandId` set together |
| 3 | Category-only (checked before brand-only) | `category` | `categoryId` set, `brandId` null |
| 4 | Brand-only | `brand` | `brandId` set, `categoryId` null |
| 5 | Global fallback | `global` | *(no rule — falls to `TaxSetting.rate`)* |

Category tiers walk the category tree (self → parent → grandparent, max 5 levels), so a rule on a
parent category still matches products in a child category if nothing more specific exists.
A `TaxRule` **cannot** mix `productId` with `categoryId`/`brandId` — a product rule always stands alone.

### `PartTaxRule` precedence (parts) — 8 tiers, same "most specific wins" idea, one more dimension (partType)
| # | Tier | `taxSource` value | Rule shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Specific part | `part-specific` | `partId` set, category/brand/type null (mirrors `TaxRule`'s productId tier) |
| 2 | Category + brand + type | `part-category+brand+type` | all three set |
| 3 | Category + brand | `part-category+brand` | category + brand set, type null |
| 4 | Brand + type | `part-brand+type` | brand + type set, category null |
| 5 | Category + type | `part-category+type` | category + type set, brand null |
| 6 | Brand-only | `part-brand` | brand set only |
| 7 | Category-only | `part-category` | category set only |
| 8 | Type-only | `part-type` | partType set only |
| — | Global fallback | `global` | *(no rule — same `TaxSetting.rate` products use)* |

Same mutual-exclusivity rule as `TaxRule`: a `PartTaxRule`'s `partId` **cannot** be combined with
`categoryId`/`brandId`/`partTypeId` — a part-specific rule always stands alone, since the part
already implies its own category/brand/type. (`PartMarkupRule`, the pricing-side equivalent, still
has no per-part scope — this per-part tier exists only for tax.)

If the global `enabled` flag is off, nothing is charged anywhere for products OR parts — it's the
master switch, overriding every active rule in both tables. A matched rule (from either table)
REPLACES the global rate for that line, it never stacks with it.

### The per-line calculation (identical for product and part lines)
```
lineDiscount = (lineTotal / subtotal) × discountAmount     (order-level discount, prorated)
taxableBase  = max(0, lineTotal − lineDiscount)
lineTax      = enabled ? round(taxableBase × resolvedRate/100) : 0
order.taxAmount = sum(lineTax across all lines)
```
The discount is spread proportionally across every line first — product or part, doesn't matter —
and only then does that line's own resolved rate get applied to what's left of it.

### Where it applies
- **Cart** (`GET /cart`, add/update/remove): returns an ESTIMATE — each item carries its own
  resolved `taxRate`/`taxAmount`/`taxSource`, plus cart-level `estimatedTax`
  (sum of all lines) and a tax-inclusive `estimatedTotal`. Applied at response time from the
  current `TaxRule`/`PartTaxRule`/`TaxSetting` state, so a rate change shows immediately (nothing
  stale is cached).
- **Checkout** (`POST /orders`, manual checkout): the server RECOMPUTES tax authoritatively per
  line (routing each to the correct engine) and snapshots `taxRate`/`taxAmount`/`taxSource` onto
  each order item (and the sum onto the order). **Never send a tax amount from the client** — it is
  ignored; the returned order's `taxAmount`/`totalAmount` are the source of truth.
- **Invoices**: inherit tax by summing each item's own snapshotted `taxAmount` when an order is
  split into INHOUSE/OUTSOURCED invoices — not a proportional estimate, since different items in
  the split can carry different resolved rates (and different engines).

### Changing a rate (global, a `TaxRule`, or a `PartTaxRule`)
Only affects NEW carts/orders. Existing orders keep the tax snapshotted at their creation time.

---

## Worked example — a mixed cart, one product line and one part line

Setup: global tax enabled at 7.5%. `TaxRule` on category "Laptops" → 10%.
`PartTaxRule` on category "RAM" → 5%.

Cart: a Dell Laptop (a real product, ₦500,000) and a Corsair RAM stick (a **part**, ₦45,000).

**`GET /api/v1/cart`** → each line resolves independently, against its own engine:
```json
{
  "subtotalAmount": 545000,
  "estimatedTax": 52250,
  "estimatedTotal": 597250,
  "items": [
    { "productName": "Dell Laptop",     "lineTotal": 500000, "taxRate": 10.0, "taxAmount": 50000, "taxSource": "category" },
    { "productName": "Corsair RAM 32GB", "lineTotal": 45000,  "taxRate": 5.0,  "taxAmount": 2250,  "taxSource": "part-category" }
  ]
}
```
Notice the RAM line's `taxSource` is `part-category`, not `category` — that prefix is how the
frontend (or a support agent reading an order) can tell at a glance which engine produced the rate,
without needing to know the line is a part at all.

**`POST /api/v1/orders`** → server recomputes the same way and snapshots it onto each `OrderItem`;
a later edit to either rule table never changes this order.

## Admin: managing the rules
Two parallel CRUD surfaces, identical shape, different table underneath:
- **Product rules**: `GET/POST /api/v1/tax/rules`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/tax/rules/{ruleId}`
- **Part rules**: `GET/POST /api/v1/tax/part-rules`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/tax/part-rules/{ruleId}`

Both require the `tax:manage` permission. Neither recomputes or stamps anything when you edit a
rule — unlike markup rules, tax is resolved live at checkout time from whatever rules are active
*then*, so an update only affects carts/orders created after it, with nothing to "reapply."

## Frontend checklist
- **Customer-facing**: show a tax line when `taxRate > 0` (from `GET /cart` or `GET /tax`), or
  per item using `item.taxRate`/`item.taxSource` for a "why was this taxed differently" breakdown.
  Display the cart's `estimatedTotal` pre-checkout. After `POST /orders`, display the order's
  `taxAmount`/`totalAmount` as final. **Never send a tax value.**
- **Admin — two separate rule tables in the UI**, mirroring the product/part markup rule screens
  you already have: a "Product tax rules" table backed by `/tax/rules` (scope = exact product OR
  category/brand), and a "Part tax rules" table backed by `/tax/part-rules` (scope = exact part OR
  category/brand/partType). Don't merge them into one form — the payloads differ (`productId` vs `partId`/`partTypeId`).
- When rendering a resolved `taxSource` anywhere (order detail, cart line), a value starting with
  `part-` came from `PartTaxRule`; anything else (`product`, `category+brand`, `category`, `brand`,
  `global`, `disabled`) came from `TaxRule` or the global setting.

*This endpoint is documentation only — there is nothing to call.*

get.summary: How live-chat allocation works (read me first)
get.description:
## Live-chat allocation model

Chats are **claimed manually from a shared queue** — there is no auto-assignment / round-robin. A chat always belongs to exactly one agent (or nobody, while it waits).

### Lifecycle

1. **A customer starts a chat** → it enters the **queue** as `WAITING`, unassigned. It appears on every agent's dashboard (socket `chat:new-conversation`).
2. **Any agent claims it** → emit socket `chat:conversation:assign-self` with the `conversationId`. The chat becomes `ACTIVE`, assigned to that agent, and leaves the queue for everyone (socket `chat:conversation:assigned` is broadcast to all staff). It now shows in that agent's **Mine**.
3. **The owner chats with the customer.** Only the owner can send messages.
4. **Resolve** → the chat closes and the agent is freed. Nothing is redistributed.

### The three staff views (REST)

| View | Endpoint | Contains |
|------|----------|----------|
| **Mine**  | `GET /conversations/mine`  | only chats assigned to **you** |
| **Queue** | `GET /conversations/queue` | unassigned `WAITING` chats — pick any |
| **All**   | `GET /conversations`       | every chat + owner — **read-only** |

### Who can respond

- An agent can **see** every chat (the *All* view) but can only **respond** to chats in their *Mine*. Attempting to reply to someone else's chat returns a socket `chat:error`.
- **Claiming** only works on **unassigned** queue chats — you cannot take a chat already owned by another agent.
- To move an owned chat to a different agent, an **admin** (SUPER_ADMIN) uses `PATCH /conversations/{id}/assign`. That is the only way ownership changes hands.

### Sticky ownership

Assignment survives disconnects: if the owning agent goes offline, the chat **stays in their Mine** (it does not fall back to the queue). It moves only when the agent returns or an admin reassigns it.

*This endpoint is documentation only — there is nothing to call.*

## AI first responder

A Claude-backed AI service (built into this backend — see `src/shared/services/ai-brain.service.ts`) can answer a new/unclaimed live chat automatically, before any staff member picks it up, including looking up real products from the catalogue. **The frontend does not trigger any of this — it happens entirely server-side** and is fully transparent to both the customer and staff apps. This page covers what each app needs to *render*, not anything it needs to *call*.

### Master switch

Controlled by the `AI_ENABLED` environment variable on the backend. When `false` (the default), behavior is byte-identical to before this feature existed — nothing calls out, nothing triggers, every conversation's `aiState` is `OFF`.

### Lifecycle — `aiState`

Every live-chat conversation carries an `aiState` field (see `ConversationListItem`/`ConversationDetail`), one of:

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `HANDLING` | The AI is answering (or will, once the next customer message arrives). No staff member has claimed the conversation. |
| `ESCALATED` | The AI handed the conversation to a human — see `aiEscalationReason` — and will **not** reply again until the conversation is `RESOLVED`. |
| `OFF` | The AI never engaged this conversation (`AI_ENABLED` was off when it started, or it was already staff-assigned/resolved). |

A staff member can claim a `HANDLING` conversation at any time via the normal `chat:assign` flow — claiming it does not change `aiState` directly, but the AI trigger condition (see below) stops matching once `assignedStaffId` is set, so it goes quiet naturally.

`aiState` changes are pushed live via the `chat:ai:state` socket event (see the server-events reference) — listen for it to move a dashboard row from "AI handling" to "Needs human" without a refetch.

### What escalation looks like on the wire

When the AI escalates, two things happen in the same moment:
1. `aiState` flips to `ESCALATED` and `chat:ai:state` fires.
2. A staff-only handover message is posted (`isInternal: true`, `senderType: "SYSTEM"`) with body `[AI handover · {reason}]\n{summary}` — this is what tells staff *why*, right in the message thread.

`aiEscalationReason` is one of `CUSTOMER_REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED_TOPIC`, `CANNOT_ANSWER`, `FRUSTRATION`, `REPLY_CAP` (hit the per-conversation reply limit), or `ERROR` (the AI service failed or isn't configured — the customer still gets a normal reply first, see below).

One `CANNOT_ANSWER` case is worth knowing about specifically: the AI has output guardrails that suppress any reply that looks like a leaked instruction, internal tool name, or code block, and escalate instead of ever sending it. A handover note whose summary reads *"Automated guardrail suppressed a suspicious model response — please review the transcript"* means this fired — usually because a customer tried to prompt-inject the bot. Expected, working-as-intended behavior, not a bug.

### Rendering an AI message

An AI-authored reply arrives as an ordinary `chat:message:received` event with `senderType: "SYSTEM"`, `senderId: "ai-assistant"`, and `senderName`/`senderAvatar` from the backend's `AI_SENDER_NAME`/`AI_SENDER_AVATAR` config (default sender name: `"Blessing Assistant"`). Render it distinctly from a `STAFF` message if you like (a bot icon, a label) — nothing on the wire requires special handling beyond recognizing the `SYSTEM` sender type, which the schema has always allowed.

**Product answers may contain a real link, as plain text.** When a customer asks about a product, the AI looks it up in the live catalogue and replies with the name, price, availability, and a URL (e.g. `https://www.blessingcomputers.com/product/dell-xps-13`) — it's just part of the `body` string, not a special token or structured field. Auto-linkify bare URLs in your message renderer (or at minimum make sure a long URL doesn't break the bubble layout) so these are actually clickable.

**Shadow mode is the one case that needs real attention.** Controlled by `AI_SHADOW_MODE` (defaults `true`): while on, an AI reply is posted with `isInternal: true` — visible to staff only, **never delivered to the customer**, so staff can review AI output before it goes live for real. A naive staff UI might show every message it receives as "sent" — if you display internal AI messages, mark them clearly (e.g. "Shadow mode — not visible to customer") so staff don't assume the customer saw it. When shadow mode is off, a genuine reply is always public; the only *forced*-public exception is the guaranteed fallback message below, which is public even during shadow mode, since a customer who was promised a reply must actually get one.

### If the AI service is unreachable or misconfigured

If `AI_REPLY_URL` isn't set, the internal Claude-backed endpoint errors (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` missing), or the call times out, the flow still completes end-to-end rather than going silent: a typing indicator appears and stops, a fallback message (`AI_FALLBACK_MESSAGE` env var) is posted **publicly** regardless of shadow mode, and the conversation escalates with reason `ERROR`. Useful when testing: this means the full plumbing — typing indicator, message delivery, escalation — behaves correctly even if the Claude side is temporarily broken or not yet configured on a given environment.

### Typing indicator

`chat:typing:start` for an AI-originated reply carries `senderName` (e.g. `"Blessing Assistant"`) instead of `userId`/`audience` — a synthetic indicator reusing the same event rather than a parallel one. Don't assume `userId`/`audience` are always present on this event.

*This endpoint is documentation only — there is nothing to call.*

get.description:
## Events emitted by the frontend

Use `socket.emit(eventName, payload)` for all events below.

---

### `chat:start` — Start a conversation
**Who:** Customer only
Only one active conversation per customer is allowed. If one already exists, the server returns it instead of creating a new one.

**Payload:**
```json
{
  "initialMessage": "Hi, I need help with my order",  // required
  "subject": "Order #12345 delayed",                   // optional
  "pageUrl": "https://shop.com/orders/12345"           // optional
}
```
**Response:** Server emits `chat:conversation:created` back to the customer.

---

### `chat:message` — Send a message
**Who:** Customer + Staff
Hot path — Redis only. Zero database calls on send. DB write is queued asynchronously.
**Rate limit:** 30 messages per minute per user.

**Payload:**
```json
{
  "conversationId": "uuid",               // required — the internal UUID (id field, not conversationId)
  "body": "When will my order arrive?",   // required
  "isInternal": false,                    // optional — staff only; hides message from customer
  "idempotencyKey": "uuid"               // optional — prevents duplicates on retry
}
```
**Response:** Sender receives `chat:message:saved`; all other room members receive `chat:message:received`.

---

### `chat:join` — Join a conversation room
**Who:** Staff only
Staff **must** emit this before they can receive `chat:message:received` for a conversation. Emit every time a conversation is opened in the UI.

**Payload:**
```json
{ "conversationId": "uuid" }
```
No response event is emitted.

---

### `chat:assign` — Self-assign a conversation
**Who:** Staff only
Staff claims a conversation for themselves. Updates DB and Redis cache, then emits `chat:conversation:assigned` to the conversation room.

**Payload:**
```json
{ "conversationId": "uuid" }
```

---

### `chat:resolve` — Resolve a conversation
**Who:** Staff only
Closes the conversation (sets status to `RESOLVED`). Emits `chat:conversation:resolved` to the conversation room and directly to the customer's personal room.

**Payload:**
```json
{ "conversationId": "uuid" }
```

---

### `chat:typing:start` / `chat:typing:stop` — Typing indicators
**Who:** Customer + Staff
Broadcasts a typing indicator to other participants. The server auto-clears after 5 seconds if `chat:typing:stop` is missed.

**Payload (both events):**
```json
{ "conversationId": "uuid" }
```

---

### `chat:read` — Mark conversation as read
**Who:** Customer + Staff
Resets the unread counter (`unreadByStaff` or `unreadByCustomer`) to zero in the database.

**Payload:**
```json
{ "conversationId": "uuid" }
```

---

### `chat:notes:update` — Update internal CRM notes
**Who:** Staff only
Creates or updates CRM notes on a conversation. All fields are optional except `conversationId`.

**Payload:**
```json
{
  "conversationId": "uuid",
  "leadName": "Jane Doe",
  "leadEmail": "jane@example.com",
  "leadPhone": "+2348012345678",
  "leadAddress": "123 Main St, Lagos",
  "leadStatus": "QUALIFIED",
  "productsDiscussed": "MacBook Pro 14, iPhone 15",
  "pricesDiscussed": "₦850,000 for MacBook",
  "budgetRange": "₦500,000 – ₦900,000",
  "customerIntent": "Wants to buy for a home office setup",
  "handoverNotes": "Follow up on Thursday, customer requested a quote",
  "followUpDate": "2024-01-18T09:00:00.000Z",
  "followUpNote": "Send pricing sheet and availability"
}
```
**leadStatus values:** `NEW` | `CONTACTED` | `QUALIFIED` | `CONVERTED` | `LOST`
**Response:** Server emits `chat:notes:updated` to the sender with `saved: true`.

---

### `staffroom:message` — Send a staff room message
**Who:** Staff only
Broadcasts a message to all connected staff. Persisted to the database asynchronously.

**Payload:**
```json
{
  "body": "Heads up — customer in CONV-ABC is escalating",
  "idempotencyKey": "uuid"  // optional
}
```

---

### `chat:conversation:created`
**Who receives:** The customer who called `chat:start`

```json
{
  "conversationId": "uuid",          // internal UUID — store this, use in all future socket events
  "publicId": "CONV-AB12CD34EF",     // human-readable — display to user
  "status": "WAITING",               // "WAITING" | "ACTIVE"
  "isExisting": false                // true if the customer already had an open conversation

```

### `chat:conversation:assigned`
**Who receives:** Everyone in the conversation room + the assigned staff member's personal room (`user:{staffId}`)

Emitted when the system (round-robin) or a staff member (`chat:assign`) assigns the conversation.

```json
{
  "conversationId": "uuid",
  "assignedStaffId": "uuid"
}
```

**Who receives:** Everyone in the conversation room + the customer's personal room

```json
  "conversationId": "uuid",
  "resolvedBy": "staffId"   // omitted in the personal-room copy sent to the customer
}
```

**Who receives:** Customer only — sent on socket connect if they have an active conversation

Allows the UI to restore state without a REST call.

```json
{
  "conversationId": "uuid",
  "publicId": "CONV-AB12CD34EF",
  "status": "WAITING" | "ACTIVE"
```

**Who receives:** `staff:room` (all connected staff) + the conversation's staff-only room. Never sent to the customer.

Fired whenever the AI first responder hands a conversation to a human, or is force-stopped (e.g. hit the reply cap). See `GET /chat/how-ai-first-responder-works` for the full lifecycle. **Who receives:** All participants in the conversation room except the sender. Internal messages (`isInternal: true`) are only delivered to staff.

```json
  "id": "uuid",
  "conversationId": "uuid",
  "senderId": "uuid",
  "senderType": "CUSTOMER" | "STAFF" | "SYSTEM",
  "senderName": "Jane Doe",
  "senderAvatar": "https://..." | null,

  "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z",
  "idempotencyKey": "msg:uuid"
```

`senderType: "SYSTEM"` is the AI first responder (`senderId: "ai-assistant"`) — see `GET /chat/how-ai-first-responder-works` for how to render it and why `isInternal: true` on a SYSTEM message (shadow mode) needs a visible "not sent to customer" cue in staff UIs.

### `chat:error`
**Who receives:** The sender of the failed event

Always listen for this to handle failures gracefully.

```json

```

**Common error messages:**

| Message | Cause |
|---------|-------|
| `"Message cannot be empty"` | Empty body in `chat:message` or `chat:start` |
| `"Too many messages — slow down"` | 30/min rate limit exceeded |
| `"Conversation not found"` | Invalid or expired conversationId |
| `"Conversation is resolved"` | Attempted to message a closed conversation |
| `"Access denied"` | Customer tried to message a conversation they don't own |
| `"Customers only"` | Staff called `chat:start` |
| `"Staff only"` | Customer called a staff-only event |
| `"Conversation not available"` | Conversation is resolved or missing (on `chat:assign`) |

## End-to-End Flows

---

## Customer Flow

```
1. Page load
   → GET /api/v1/chat/my-conversation      (restore history if a conversation exists)

2. Connect socket
   io('/ws', { auth: { token } })
   ← chat:conversation:updated             (if existing conversation — socket auto-joined to room)

3. Start a new chat
   → chat:start { initialMessage, subject?, pageUrl? }
   ← chat:conversation:created { conversationId, publicId, status: 'WAITING' }

4. Waiting for agent
   ← chat:queue:position { position: 2 }   (if no staff available)
   ← chat:conversation:assigned            (when a staff member is assigned)

5. Messaging
   → chat:message { conversationId, body, idempotencyKey }
   ← chat:message:saved   { idempotencyKey, tempId, createdAt }    (ack — sender only)
   ← chat:message:received { ... }                                  (staff replies)

6. Typing indicators
   → chat:typing:start { conversationId }
   → chat:typing:stop  { conversationId }
   ← chat:typing:start { conversationId, userId, audience: 'staff' }

7. Mark read
   → chat:read { conversationId }

8. Chat closed
   ← chat:conversation:resolved { conversationId }
```

---

## Staff / Admin Flow

```
1. Page load
   → GET /api/v1/chat/conversations         (load queue)

2. Connect socket
   io('/ws', { auth: { token } })
   ← presence:list                          (who is currently online)
   ← staffroom:history                      (recent staff room messages)
   → presence:heartbeat                     (start 30-second interval)

3. New chat arrives
   ← chat:dashboard:new { conversationId, publicId, customerId, preview, ... }
      → add to queue UI in real time

4. Open a conversation
   → GET /api/v1/chat/conversations/:id     (load history + notes)
   → chat:join { conversationId }           (must emit before receiving messages)

5. Self-assign (if not auto-assigned by the system)
   → chat:assign { conversationId }
   ← chat:conversation:assigned { conversationId, assignedStaffId }

6. Send a message
   → chat:message { conversationId, body }
   ← chat:message:saved                     (ack)
   ← chat:message:received                  (customer replies)

7. Send an internal note (not visible to customer)
   → chat:message { conversationId, body, isInternal: true }

8. Update CRM notes
   → chat:notes:update { conversationId, leadStatus, followUpDate, ... }
   ← chat:notes:updated { saved: true }

9. Resolve the conversation
   → chat:resolve { conversationId }
   ← chat:conversation:resolved             (broadcast to room + customer)

10. Notifications for assigned conversations
    ← notification:new { type: 'NEW_MESSAGE', conversationId, preview }
```

---

## Important: ID fields

| Field | Example | Use for |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `id` | `a1b2c3d4-e5f6...` | All socket event payloads, REST `/conversations/:id` |
| `conversationId` | `CONV-AB12CD34EF` | Display to users only — **not** for socket events |

Always use the `id` (UUID) field in socket events, not the human-readable `conversationId`.

---

## Quick verification checklist

| What to verify | How to confirm |
|----------------|----------------|
| Socket auth works | `socket.connected === true`, no `connect_error` |
| Customer starts chat | Receives `chat:conversation:created` with `conversationId` |
| Staff sees new chat | Staff socket receives `chat:dashboard:new` without refresh |
| Auto-assignment | Customer receives `chat:conversation:assigned`; staff receives it in personal room |
| Queue (no staff online) | Customer receives `chat:queue:position` with a position number |
| Messages work | Sender gets `chat:message:saved`; other side gets `chat:message:received` |
| Staff receives messages | Only works after `chat:join` is emitted for that conversation |
| Notifications | Staff personal room receives `notification:new` on new customer message |
| Resolve | Both sides receive `chat:conversation:resolved` |
| Presence | Other staff receive `presence:staff:online` when someone connects |

**Channel split.** `revenue` and `orders` are each broken into `online`, `manual`, and `combined`:

get.description:
Returns a **permission-gated, real-time KPI snapshot** for a single staff member.

### How sections are determined

Each staff member is assigned a **custom RBAC role** which carries a set of named permissions (e.g. `orders:read`, `inventory:manage`).
On every request the service:
1. Fetches the target staff's role and live permissions **from the database** (never from the JWT — permissions are always current).
2. Walks the internal `PERMISSION_SECTION_MAP` to find which KPI sections those permissions unlock.
3. Runs only the relevant DB fetchers **in parallel** and returns the merged result.

This means the `sections` object is **different for every role** — a sales agent sees orders and customers, a warehouse manager sees inventory and products, a super admin sees everything.

### Permission → section mapping

| Permission(s) | Section key in `sections` |
|---|---|
| `orders:read` / `orders:write` / `orders:manage` | `orders` |
| `payments:read` / `payments:manage` | `payments` |
| `refunds:read` / `refunds:manage` | `refunds` |
| `inventory:read` / `inventory:write` / `inventory:manage` | `inventory` |
| `products:read` / `products:write` / `products:manage` | `products` |
| `customers:read` / `customers:manage` | `customers` |
| `conversations:read` / `conversations:manage` | `conversations` |
| `invoices:read` / `invoices:write` / `invoices:approve` | `invoices` |
| `coupons:read` / `coupons:manage` | `coupons` |
| `reviews:read` / `reviews:moderate` | `reviews` |
| `staff:read` / `staff:manage` | `staff` |
| `security_logs:read` | `security` |

Multiple permissions that map to the same section key only trigger the DB fetcher **once** (de-duplicated internally).

### Access control

| Caller | Can fetch |
|---|---|
| Any active staff member | Their **own** dashboard only |
| `SUPER_ADMIN` | **Any** staff member's dashboard |

Attempting to fetch another staff member's dashboard without `SUPER_ADMIN` returns **403**.

### `:staffId` format

Accepts either:
- A DB UUID: `a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890`
- A human-readable display ID: `STF-0012345678`

### Rate limiting
**60 requests / minute** per authenticated staff member.
Remaining quota is returned in the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` response header.

Returns a **paginated, sorted** list of notifications belonging to the currently authenticated staff member. Each staff member can only see their own notifications.

### Sort order
1. Important notifications first (`isImportant: true`)
2. Newest first within each importance group

### Notification types

| Type | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `UPLOAD_TARGET_SET` | Super admin set or updated this staff member's daily upload target |
| `LOW_STOCK_ALERT` | A product variant fell below its low-stock threshold |
| `NEW_ORDER` | A new customer order was placed |
| `PRICE_CONFIRMATION_NEEDED` | An order with outsourced items needs price confirmation |
| `ORDER_STATUS_UPDATE` | An order's status changed |
| `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` / `PAYMENT_FAILED` | Payment event on an order |
| `ACCOUNT_UPDATE` | Profile or role changes |
| `SECURITY_ALERT` | Suspicious login or security event |
| `GENERAL` | System announcements — including payment reliability alerts: a payment stuck `PENDING` past 2h that the reconciliation sweep couldn't auto-resolve, and a payment job that exhausted every retry and landed in the dead-letter queue. Both are `isImportant: true` with a `link` into the relevant payment / DLQ page. |

### Recommended frontend pattern

```
1. On login / page load  →  GET /staff/notifications/unread-count  (badge number)
2. Staff opens bell icon →  GET /staff/notifications               (full list)
3. Staff taps one item   →  PATCH /staff/notifications/:id/read   (badge -1)
4. "Mark all as read"    →  PATCH /staff/notifications/read-all   (badge → 0)
```

### Real-time updates

New notifications are also pushed via Socket.IO on the `/ws` namespace. Listen for event names matching the notification type (e.g. `upload-target:set`). Refresh the unread count on each socket event.

post.description:
**The central checkout action.** Converts the customer's cart into a ManualOrder and returns the bank account details and payment instructions.

---

### Prerequisites
1. Customer must be authenticated.
2. Cart must not be empty and all items must be in stock (run `POST /cart/validate` first).
3. A phone number must exist on the customer profile **OR** be supplied in this request body.    If no phone is found anywhere, checkout is blocked with `PHONE_REQUIRED`.

---

### Delivery Methods
**DISPATCH:** Standard delivery to customer's address. Requires `shippingAddress` (saved or inline).

**SELF_PICKUP:** Customer collects in-store. NO `shippingAddress` required (will be rejected if sent). Only `billingAddress` is needed for invoicing purposes.

---

### Address Modes
For each address (shipping/billing), provide exactly one of:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `*AddressId` | UUID of a saved address from `GET /addresses` |
| `*Address` | Full inline address object (see schema) |

**Shipping address rules by delivery method:**
- `DISPATCH`: `shippingAddressId` OR `shippingAddress` **required**
- `SELF_PICKUP`: `shippingAddressId` and `shippingAddress` **must NOT be sent** (returns 400)

**Billing address rules:**
- Always required for both `DISPATCH` and `SELF_PICKUP`
- For `DISPATCH` only: Set `billingSameAsShipping: true` to skip billing fields entirely — billing mirrors shipping
- For `SELF_PICKUP`: `billingSameAsShipping` is invalid (no shipping address exists)

**`saveToAccount` in inline addresses:** If `true` (default), the inline address is persisted to the customer's address book. If `false`, a temporary one-time address is created.

---

### What Happens Next
1. Order is created with status `AWAITING_PAYMENT`.
2. Prices are **locked** at this moment — subsequent price changes do not affect this order.
3. Cart is NOT cleared yet (cleared after payment confirmation).
4. Customer transfers the exact amount and uploads proof via `POST /checkout/:manualOrderId/proof`.

---

### Stock Management
- Stock is NOT decremented at checkout (customer hasn't paid yet)
- Stock is decremented when admin confirms payment via `POST /admin/checkout/orders/:id/validate-payment`
- If order is cancelled after payment confirmation, stock is automatically restored

---

### Example Requests

**Delivery with saved addresses:**
```json
{
  "cartSessionId": "uuid",
  "deliveryMethod": "DISPATCH",
  "shippingAddressId": "uuid",
  "billingSameAsShipping": true
}
```

**Delivery with inline shipping, saved billing:**
```json
{
  "cartSessionId": "uuid",
  "deliveryMethod": "DISPATCH",
  "shippingAddress": { "firstName": "John", ... },
  "billingAddressId": "uuid"
}
```

**Self-pickup (no shipping address):**
```json
{
  "cartSessionId": "uuid",
  "deliveryMethod": "SELF_PICKUP",
  "billingAddressId": "uuid"
}
```

**`awaitingPayment`** — Count of orders with status `AWAITING_PAYMENT`
- Customer has placed order but not uploaded proof yet
- Action: Follow up with customer if needed

**`pendingReview`** — Count of orders with status `PROOF_SUBMITTED` + `PROOF_UPLOADED`
- Customer uploaded proof and waiting for admin validation
- Action: Review proof images and validate/reject
- **This is your primary work queue**

**`confirmedToday`** — Count of orders confirmed today (`validatedAt >= start of today`)
- Shows daily processing throughput
- Action: Track team productivity

- Includes `PENDING` + `PROOF_UPLOADED` payment statuses
- Shows potential revenue awaiting confirmation
- Action: Prioritize high-value order reviews

This endpoint runs 4 database queries in parallel using `Promise.all()`. Expected response time: < 200ms for typical database sizes. Safe to call frequently (e.g., every minute) without performance impact.

post.description:
**The most critical admin action.** Admin views the customer's proof of payment image, verifies the amount, and confirms the payment.

---

### What Happens on Confirmation

**Order Status Changes:**
1. `paymentStatus` → `CONFIRMED`
2. `orderStatus` → `PROCESSING`
3. `confirmedAmountPaid` is recorded (may differ slightly from `totalAmount`)
4. `validatedByStaffId` and `validatedAt` are recorded for audit trail

**Stock Management (Critical):**
5. **Stock is decremented** for each item in the order
6. Each stock change is logged in `inventory_transactions` table with:
   - `type: SALE`
   - `referenceType: MANUAL_ORDER`
   - `referenceId: manualOrderId`
   - `quantityBefore` and `quantityAfter` for audit
   - `staffId` of the admin who confirmed

**Customer Notification:**
7. Customer receives in-app notification: "Payment Confirmed ✓"
8. Status history entry created with validation timestamp

---

### Stock Safety Checks

If any item has insufficient stock at validation time:
- Returns `400 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK` error
- Transaction is rolled back (no partial stock decrements)
- Admin sees which item(s) caused the failure
- Admin can contact customer to modify order or restock item

**Example error:**
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Insufficient stock for \"MacBook Pro 14\" - Space Grey\". Available: 0, Required: 1",
  "code": "INSUFFICIENT_STOCK"
}
```

---

### Amount Discrepancy Handling

The `confirmedAmountPaid` field allows admin to record exactly what appears on the receipt, even if it differs from `totalAmount`.

**Common scenarios:**
- Customer paid NGN 1,850,000 but order total is NGN 1,849,999 (bank rounding)
- Customer overpaid by mistake
- Customer underpaid — admin can follow up before confirming

The discrepancy (`confirmedAmountPaid - totalAmount`) is logged for financial reconciliation.

---

### Audit Trail

Every confirmation creates permanent records:
- `validatedByStaffId` — who confirmed
- `validatedAt` — when confirmed
- `confirmedAmountPaid` — exact amount on receipt
- `inventory_transactions` — every stock decrement with before/after quantities

Use `GET /api/v1/admin/checkout/orders/:id` to view full audit trail.

---

### Prerequisites
- Order must be in `PROOF_SUBMITTED` status
- Proof image must be uploaded (`proofOfPaymentUrl` not null)
- All items must have sufficient stock

- Amount on receipt does not match the order total
- Receipt appears to be from a different transaction
- Receipt date is too old
- Name on receipt does not match account

**What happens on rejection:**
1. `paymentStatus` → `REJECTED`
2. `orderStatus` → `PAYMENT_REJECTED`
3. `rejectionReason` is saved
4. Customer receives an in-app notification with the exact rejection reason
5. Customer can re-upload via `POST /checkout/:manualOrderId/proof`
6. **Stock is NOT touched** (no decrement on rejection)

**The `rejectionReason` is shown directly to the customer** — write it clearly and professionally so the customer knows exactly what to fix.

patch.description:
Advances the order through fulfillment after payment is confirmed.

---

### Status Flow — Delivery Orders (DISPATCH)
```
PAYMENT_CONFIRMED
      ↓
  PROCESSING   ← admin prepares the order
      ↓
  ASSIGNED     ← rider name + phone required
      ↓
OUT_FOR_DELIVERY
      ↓
  DELIVERED    ← deliveredAt timestamp set
      ↓
  COMPLETED    ← completedAt timestamp set
```

### Status Flow — Self-Pickup Orders (SELF_PICKUP)
```
PAYMENT_CONFIRMED
      ↓
  PROCESSING   ← admin prepares order for collection
      ↓
  COMPLETED    ← customer collected, completedAt set
```

**Important:** `ASSIGNED`, `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY`, and `DELIVERED` are **invalid** for `SELF_PICKUP` orders. Attempting to set these statuses returns `400 INVALID_STATUS_FOR_SELF_PICKUP`.

---

### Field Requirements per Status
| `orderStatus` | Extra required fields | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| `ASSIGNED` | `riderName` + `riderPhone` | DISPATCH only |
| `CANCELLED` | `cancelReason` | Both |
| All others | `note` optional | Both |

---

### Stock Restoration on Cancellation/Refund

If order is cancelled or refunded **AFTER payment was confirmed:**
- **Stock is automatically restored** for all items
- Each restoration is logged in `inventory_transactions` with:
  - `type: RETURN`
  - `referenceType: MANUAL_ORDER_CANCELLED` or `MANUAL_ORDER_REFUNDED`
  - `quantityBefore` and `quantityAfter` for audit
- Transaction is atomic — all items restored or none

**Example:**
1. Admin confirms payment → stock decremented by 1
2. Customer requests cancellation
3. Admin sets `orderStatus: CANCELLED` → stock incremented by 1
4. `inventory_transactions` shows both SALE and RETURN records

If order is cancelled **BEFORE payment confirmation:**
- No stock changes (stock was never decremented)

---

### Guard — Payment Must Be Confirmed
Cannot move to any fulfillment status if `paymentStatus !== CONFIRMED`, except `CANCELLED` and `REFUNDED` which are always allowed.

---

### Customer Notifications
Every status change sends an in-app notification. Notifications are customized per delivery method:

**DISPATCH notifications:**
- `ASSIGNED`: "A rider has been assigned to deliver your order. Rider: John — 08012345678"
- `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY`: "Your order is on its way!"
- `DELIVERED`: "Your order has been delivered"

**SELF_PICKUP notifications:**
- `PROCESSING`: "Your order is being prepared. We will notify you when ready for collection"
- `COMPLETED`: "Your order is ready for collection. Thank you!"

`OUT_FOR_DELIVERY`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, and `REFUNDED` are flagged `isImportant: true` for prominent display.

| `INVALID_STATUS_FOR_SELF_PICKUP` | Trying to set ASSIGNED/OUT_FOR_DELIVERY/DELIVERED on SELF_PICKUP order |
| Validation | `riderName`/`riderPhone` missing for ASSIGNED, `cancelReason` missing for CANCELLED |

get.summary: Combined order list — online (gateway) + manual checkout, filterable
get.description:
Merges `Order` (paid through Paystack/Miden) and `ManualOrder` (manual/offline
checkout) into one paginated, filterable list — so you don't have to check `GET /api/v1/orders` and
the manual-orders admin list separately to see everything. Requires `orders:read` — the same
permission both source endpoints already use, so anyone who could already see both channels
separately can see them combined here.

### `source` filter
`ONLINE` (Order only), `MANUAL` (ManualOrder only), or `ALL` (default) — merges both, sorted
together by `sortBy`, not two separate blocks.

### `status` filter — raw value, validated against the union of both enums
Most values are shared by name between `OrderStatus` and `ManualOrderStatus`
(`PROCESSING`, `ASSIGNED`, `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY`, `DELIVERED`, `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`, `REFUNDED`) —
those filter both sources identically. Each source also has its own early-lifecycle values that only
exist on that side:
- ONLINE only: `PENDING_PRICE_CONFIRMATION`, `PRICE_CONFIRMED`, `PENDING`
- MANUAL only: `AWAITING_PAYMENT`, `PROOF_SUBMITTED`, `PAYMENT_CONFIRMED`, `PAYMENT_REJECTED`

Filtering by a value that only exists on one side returns rows from that side only (the other side
structurally cannot have any matches — not an error, just an empty contribution).

### `paymentStatus` filter — normalized, NOT the raw enum
Online's `PaymentStatus` and manual's `ManualPaymentStatus` don't share the same vocabulary for the
same real-world state (`PAID` vs `CONFIRMED`, `FAILED` vs `REJECTED`), so this filter takes a
normalized value and maps it onto each source's actual column:

| `paymentStatus` | matches ONLINE | matches MANUAL |
|---|---|---|
| `PENDING` | `PENDING` | `PENDING`, `PROOF_UPLOADED` |
| `PAID` | `PAID` | `CONFIRMED` |
| `FAILED` | `FAILED` | `REJECTED` |
| `REFUNDED` | `REFUNDED` | `REFUNDED` |

Every row in the response also carries this same normalized value as `paymentStatusNormalized`, so
the frontend can render one consistent "Paid / Pending / Failed / Refunded" badge regardless of
which table a row came from, without re-implementing this mapping client-side.

### Pagination note
`Order` and `ManualOrder` are different tables — a single SQL query can't page across both, so this
fetches enough of each source to guarantee a correct merged page, then slices it in memory. Correct
for realistic order volumes; extremely deep pagination (`page` × `limit` beyond ~1000) is capped as a
safety valve rather than built out as full cursor pagination.

### Line items
Each row includes its full `items` array (product name, SKU, quantity, unit/total price, per-line
tax snapshot) — same underlying data as `GET /api/v1/orders/{id}` (ONLINE) or the manual-orders admin
detail endpoint (MANUAL). Items are only fetched for the rows actually returned on the current page,
not for every candidate row considered while computing the correct merged sort order (which can be
much larger — see pagination note above) — so this stays cheap regardless of `page`/`limit`.

phone on a specific address, not the customer's own profile phone.

connected OAuth providers, etc.) see `GET /api/auth/customer/me`, which this endpoint does not
replace.
