get.summary: How the WhatsApp module works (read me first)
get.description:
## Overview

This module is a **standalone** WhatsApp Business integration — it does not share tables, queues, workers, or Socket.IO rooms/events with live chat (`/api/v1/chat`). It reuses the same authenticated `/ws` Socket.IO namespace only as transport, and reuses the app-wide generic notification bell for one thing (see "Notifications" below).

Built on Meta's **WhatsApp Cloud API**. Messaging-only scope: no template/broadcast sending, no campaigns — just customer ↔ agent conversations, the same way live chat works.

## Allocation model — same as live chat, NOT round-robin

Conversations are **claimed manually from a shared queue**. There is no auto-assignment: a WhatsApp round-robin allocator exists in the codebase (`WhatsAppAllocationService`) but is never triggered by the live flow, deliberately — the same way live chat's own round-robin machinery sits unused. Auto-push-assigning every new conversation to "whoever happens to be online" just floods that one agent; a shared queue lets the whole team pick up work as they free up.

### Lifecycle

1. **A customer messages your WhatsApp number** → the conversation is created as `WAITING`, unassigned. It's broadcast to every WhatsApp-available staff member's dashboard (socket `whatsapp:conversation:new`).
2. **Any WhatsApp-available agent claims it** → `POST /conversations/{id}/assign-self`. The conversation becomes `ACTIVE`, assigned to that agent, and leaves the queue for everyone (socket `whatsapp:conversation:assigned` broadcasts to all staff).
3. **The owner replies from the dashboard** — see "Sending a reply" below for what happens on the customer's phone.
4. **Resolve** → `POST /conversations/{id}/resolve`. Nothing is redistributed.

An admin can move an already-claimed conversation to a different agent at any time: `PATCH /conversations/{id}/assign` (**SUPER_ADMIN only**) — the only way ownership changes hands other than a fresh claim.

## WhatsApp presence is independent of chat presence

A staff member does **not** automatically enter the WhatsApp pool by opening the dashboard or being online for live chat. They must explicitly toggle `POST /presence/online` to receive WhatsApp conversations, and `POST /presence/offline` to stop. This lets an agent handle live chat without being pulled into WhatsApp, and vice versa.

## Does the customer get a normal WhatsApp notification when an agent replies?

**Yes — exactly like a normal WhatsApp message from any contact.** When an agent sends a reply (`POST /conversations/{id}/messages`), it goes out through Meta's Graph API to the customer's real WhatsApp number. On the customer's phone this is indistinguishable from any other WhatsApp message: it lands in their normal chat thread with your business number, triggers the standard WhatsApp push notification (banner + sound, subject to their own notification settings), and shows up with delivery/read ticks. There is no separate "in-app" notification system for the customer side — WhatsApp's own infrastructure handles that end entirely.

**The one hard constraint:** Meta only allows a free-form reply within **24 hours of the customer's last message** (`windowExpiresAt` on the conversation). Outside that window, `POST /conversations/{id}/messages` returns `422 WHATSAPP_WINDOW_CLOSED` instead of silently failing — **build the UI to disable/hide the reply box and show this state** once the window has passed. This module deliberately does not implement Meta's pre-approved "template message" workaround for messaging outside the window (out of scope — messaging-only).

## Notifications on the admin dashboard

Two independent things fire the moment a customer message arrives:
1. **Notification bell** (`notification:new` on the shared `/ws` namespace, `user:{staffId}` room) — the same generic bell used elsewhere in the app (e.g. invoices). Fires for the assigned agent on every new message, and for the drainer once a conversation is assigned.
2. **Live inbox update** (`whatsapp:*` events, described in the Socket.IO reference below) — updates the conversation list/thread view in real time without a page refresh.

## Customer phone number visibility

Every conversation is keyed by `waId` — the customer's **real WhatsApp phone number** (e.g. `2348012345678`, E.164 without the `+`). This is returned in full on every endpoint that lists or fetches a conversation (`GET /conversations`, `GET /conversations/queue`, `GET /conversations/{id}`).

This is inherent to WhatsApp, not something masked or optional — replying to a customer means sending to their real number, so the number has to be visible somewhere in the flow. A few things to design the UI around:

- **Any staff member can see it, not just the assigned agent.** `GET /conversations` is a read-only overview of *every* conversation (same model as live chat's "watch other agents' chats" view) — it includes `waId` for conversations that aren't assigned to the caller too. There is currently **no restriction** hiding the number from non-owning staff.
- Also visible: `profileName` — the customer's own WhatsApp display name (whatever they've set on their phone), shown the same way it would appear in a personal WhatsApp contact list if not saved.
- If you want number visibility restricted (e.g. only the assigned agent sees the full number, or it's masked like `234801****678` for everyone else in the overview list), that access-control layer does not exist yet and would need to be added on top of this — flag it if that's a requirement before launch.

*This endpoint is documentation only — there is nothing to call.*

get.summary: Server → Client events (what the dashboard listens for)
get.description:
## Events emitted by the server

Same `/ws` namespace and auth as live chat (see the Chat docs for the socket connection/auth setup — it's shared infrastructure, not chat-specific). Use `socket.on(eventName, callback)` for all events below.

---

### `whatsapp:conversation:new`
**Who receives:** every staff socket currently in `wa:staff:room` (i.e. everyone toggled online for WhatsApp)

Emitted the moment a brand-new WhatsApp conversation is created (first message from a number that's never messaged before).

```json
{
  "conversationId": "uuid",
  "waId": "2348012345678",
  "profileName": "Jane Doe",
  "preview": "Hi, do you have this in stock..."
}
```

---

### `whatsapp:conversation:assigned`
**Who receives:** the conversation's socket room (`wa:conv:{id}`), the newly-assigned staff member's personal room (`user:{staffId}`), and `wa:staff:room`

Fired by both a self-claim and an admin reassign.

```json
{ "conversationId": "uuid", "assignedStaffId": "uuid" }
```

---

### `whatsapp:conversation:resolved`
**Who receives:** `wa:conv:{id}` and `wa:staff:room`

```json
{ "conversationId": "uuid" }
```

---

### `whatsapp:message:new`
**Who receives:** `wa:conv:{id}`; also broadcast to `wa:staff:room` if the conversation is still unassigned (so the waiting-queue preview updates live)

Fired for both inbound (customer) and outbound (staff) messages.

```json
{
  "conversationId": "uuid",
  "assignedStaffId": "uuid" | null,
  "waId": "2348012345678",
  "profileName": "Jane Doe",
  "body": "Hi, do you have this in stock?",
  "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"
}
```

---

### `whatsapp:message:status`
**Who receives:** `wa:staff:room` — the frontend matches by `waMessageId` against whichever thread is open

Delivery-status ticks for outbound messages, driven by Meta's status webhooks.

```json
{ "waMessageId": "wamid.HBg...", "status": "SENT" | "DELIVERED" | "READ" | "FAILED" }
```

---

### `whatsapp:queue:position`
**Who receives:** `wa:conv:{id}` — only relevant if you ever re-enable the dormant round-robin path; unused in the current claim-based flow

### `whatsapp:presence:heartbeat`
**Who:** Staff only
No payload. Send every ~30s while toggled online for WhatsApp to keep the presence TTL alive. (There's also a REST equivalent, `POST /presence/heartbeat` — use whichever fits your client's architecture, not both.)

## Admin Dashboard Flow

```
1. Page load
   → GET /api/v1/whatsapp/conversations/queue    (unassigned, claimable)
   → GET /api/v1/whatsapp/conversations?mine=true (my active conversations)

2. Connect socket (shared /ws namespace — same auth as chat)
   io('/ws', { auth: { token } })

3. Go online for WhatsApp
   → POST /api/v1/whatsapp/presence/online
   → whatsapp:presence:heartbeat                  (start ~30s interval)
   or → POST /presence/heartbeat on the same interval

4. New conversation arrives
   ← whatsapp:conversation:new { conversationId, waId, profileName, preview }
      → add a row to the queue UI in real time

5. Claim it
   → POST /api/v1/whatsapp/conversations/{id}/assign-self
   ← whatsapp:conversation:assigned { conversationId, assignedStaffId }
      → moves from the queue view into "mine"

6. Open the thread
   → GET /api/v1/whatsapp/conversations/{id}      (history + windowExpiresAt)
   → whatsapp:join_conversation { conversationId }

7. Reply
   → POST /api/v1/whatsapp/conversations/{id}/messages { body }
   ← whatsapp:message:new { ... }                 (live echo once sent)
   ← whatsapp:message:status { waMessageId, status: 'DELIVERED' }  (then 'READ')

   If windowExpiresAt has passed:
   ← 422 { code: 'WHATSAPP_WINDOW_CLOSED' }        (disable the reply box instead of showing a raw error)

8. Customer replies
   ← whatsapp:message:new { ... }
   ← notification:new { type: 'NEW_MESSAGE', conversationId, preview, channel: 'whatsapp' }

9. Resolve
   → POST /api/v1/whatsapp/conversations/{id}/resolve
   ← whatsapp:conversation:resolved { conversationId }

10. Admin reassigns someone else's conversation
    → PATCH /api/v1/whatsapp/conversations/{id}/assign { staffId }   (SUPER_ADMIN only)
    ← whatsapp:conversation:assigned { conversationId, assignedStaffId }
```

| `id` | `a1b2c3d4-e5f6...` | All socket event payloads, REST `/conversations/:id` |
| `conversationId` | `WA-AB12CD34EF` | Display to users only — **not** for socket events |

## Quick verification checklist

| What to verify | How to confirm |
|----------------|----------------|
| Socket auth works | `socket.connected === true`, no `connect_error` |
| Going online works | `POST /presence/online` then `GET /presence/me` shows `isOnline: true` |
| New conversation reaches everyone online | All online-for-WhatsApp staff sockets receive `whatsapp:conversation:new` without a refresh |
| Claim works, no auto-assignment | Conversation stays in `/conversations/queue` until someone calls assign-self — never assigned automatically |
| Reply reaches the real phone | Send a reply; the test WhatsApp number receives a normal push notification within a few seconds |
| Window enforcement | Sending after 24h of silence from the customer returns 422 `WHATSAPP_WINDOW_CLOSED` |
| Delivery ticks | `whatsapp:message:status` fires SENT → DELIVERED → (READ if the customer opens it) |
| Reassign | SUPER_ADMIN `PATCH .../assign` moves the conversation; the new owner's socket receives `whatsapp:conversation:assigned` |

## How the Promotions system works

A **Promotion** is a named campaign (e.g. "Back-to-School Sale") that holds one or more **Slides**. Each slide is a single image with an optional caption and product link. The frontend renders these as a homepage banner or carousel.

### Staff workflow (admin dashboard)

```
1. POST /api/v1/promotions          → create promotion shell (starts as DRAFT)
2. POST /api/v1/promotions/:id/slides → upload images + attach product links
3. POST /api/v1/promotions/:id/publish → make it live on the website
4. (later) POST /api/v1/promotions/:id/archive → take it offline, keep history
```

### Frontend rendering workflow

```
GET /api/v1/promotions              → fetch all PUBLISHED promotions (no auth)
  └─ response includes slides[]    → each slide has imageUrl, description, productSlug
        └─ productSlug             → build link to /products/{productSlug}
        └─ externalUrl             → or link to an external page
        └─ productId               → alternative to slug if the UI uses UUIDs
```

### Slide link fields — pick one per slide

| Field | When to use |
|---|---|
| `productSlug` | Internal product page — build the link as `/products/{productSlug}` |
| `productId` | If the frontend uses UUID-based routing instead of slugs |
| `externalUrl` | External pages, campaign landing pages, or partner URLs |

All three can be null if the slide is decorative only.

### Status lifecycle

| Status | Visible to public? | Who can set it |
|---|---|---|
| `DRAFT` | No | Created automatically |
| `PUBLISHED` | Yes | `promotions:publish` permission |
| `ARCHIVED` | No | `promotions:publish` permission |

Upload one or more images for a promotion. Each image becomes one slide and can carry its own caption and product link.

**Content-Type:** `multipart/form-data`

### Form fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `files` | file (repeatable) | Yes | Images — JPEG/PNG/WebP only, max **5 MB** each, max **20 files** per request |
| `metadata` | string (JSON) | No | JSON array of metadata objects, **one per file in the same order**. If omitted, slides are created with no captions or links. |

### metadata format

The `metadata` field must be a JSON-encoded array where index 0 matches the first file, index 1 the second, and so on. Each object is:

```json
[
  {
    "description": "Dell XPS 15 at ₦499,000 — back-to-school special",
    "productSlug": "dell-xps-15-2024"
  },
  {
    "description": "HP Envy 360 bundle",
    "productId": "3f6c1234-...",
    "externalUrl": null
  },
  {
    "description": null
  }
]
```

All fields inside each metadata entry are optional. Missing entries default to nulls (safe to send a shorter array than the number of files).

### What happens to the images

1. Images are compressed server-side (converted to WebP, max-width 1920px).
2. Uploaded to Cloudinary or S3 depending on the server's `STORAGE_PROVIDER` setting.
3. New slides are appended **after** any existing slides on this promotion — they do not replace existing ones.
4. Each slide gets an auto-incremented `order` value (can be changed later with PATCH).

Requires **`promotions:write`**.
